dct_description_sm: The program MERGE brings together seven laboratories in Canada to apply molecular and classical techniques to high Arctic Canada (northern Nunavut), and to work in concert with the international IPY community to address fundamental questions in polar biodiversity. Specifically, the funding is allowing Canada to be a full partner and leading participant in the IPY program MERGE: 'Microbiological and Ecological Responses to Global Environmental Changes in Polar Regions'. Our Canadian research focuses on the microbial richness at three Arctic sites that have analogues in Antarctica: lakes, fiords, ice shelves, springs and permafrost soils on Ellesmere Island, Axel Heiberg Island and Bylot Island, with comparative information in subarctic Qubec. The team is composed of leading specialists in viruses, heterotrophic bacteria, archaea, cyanobacteria and microbial eukaryotes, as the microbiota likely dominate the total biodiversity as well as total community biomass of polar desert regions. The international IPY collaboration is allowing us to place our discoveries in a bi-polar context and is an exciting opportunity to address global hypotheses concerning microbial dispersal, cosmopolitanism, bio-geography and endemism.
dct_title_s: Microbiological and Ecological Responses to Global Environmental change in the polar regions (MERGE)
